interpretation: Measurement design, not estimator sophistication, sets what is recoverable: identifiability is a rank property of the Poisson-weighted Jacobian (F-001). This is direct evidence for H2 (Q-003) in the idealised regime. Two error classes behave differently: basis misspecification is systematic and dose-independent (F-003), whereas spectral mismatch at these magnitudes is design-dependent and can hide below the noise floor (F-004). A learned method cannot repair a rank-deficient design; comparisons of learned methods must therefore be made within an identifiable design or they measure the prior, not the physics.
limitations: Idealised 2D toy: 48x48 pixels, parallel beam, additive mixtures with no volume conservation, Poisson-only noise, no scatter/detector blur/pile-up/beam hardening correction. Statistics on a ray subset, not the full image. Shared forward model for data and estimator (no inverse crime avoidance): this is a best case and overstates achievable accuracy. D-002: iodine K-edge under-resolved on the 1 keV table, so NO absolute iodine-concentration claim is made. Elemental reference densities, not tissue mixtures. CPU/MPS laptop only; nothing here validates GPU or HPC. Absolute spectrum normalisation UNVERIFIED (designs compared at equal photons per ray by construction).
next_experiment: EXP-003: spectral-mismatch power study. Sweep perturbation magnitude (tilt 0 to 30%, energy scale 0 to 5%) at fixed design, with realisation count chosen from a pre-computed power analysis so the detection floor is known BEFORE running, and an analytic bias prediction from first-order perturbation of the MLE to compare against. This resolves F-004 and is the prerequisite for any inverse-crime-free comparison under H1.
unresolved: Whether dual-kVp is genuinely insensitive to smooth spectral error or (f) was merely under-powered. Whether the K-edge-resolved table (T-006) changes iodine conditioning. How conclusions move under a mismatched forward model (the inverse-crime-free setting of H1/Q-002).
what_failed: Prediction (f) partially falsified (F-004): dual-kVp cells on the 2-material phantom showed mismatch bias only 0.73-1.77x their noise floor, i.e. not detectably biased, while photon-counting designs showed 6-8x. The pre-registered criterion assumed all mismatch produces detectable bias; at the chosen perturbation sizes and 20 realisations it is under-powered for dual-kVp. Under-power vs genuine insensitivity is NOT resolved by this experiment.
what_happened: RUN-0002 (clean tree, commit cf3b880, 71s CPU): 42 cells over phantoms P2/P3 x designs M1/M2/M4 x k in {2,3} x N_tot in {1e5,1e6} x matched/4 mismatch conditions. Per-ray Fisher/CRLB/rank/empirical statistics on a seeded ray subset (48 rays P2, 60 P3; 20 Poisson realisations each); 16 full-image reconstructions (90x72 rays, 1 realisation each). Pre-registered predictions: (a)-(e) and (g) PASS, (f) FAILS 5 of 12 cells. STOP condition not triggered.
what_worked: Rank/identifiability predictions exactly as pre-registered. Empirical std matched CRLB within 11% for all identifiable cells at 1e6 photons (F-002), validating forward model + Jacobian + estimator as a consistent stack. Zero LM convergence failures across all cells. Byte-identical metrics on re-run.

interpretation: The durable scientific content is narrower than first stated. Measurement design sets what is recoverable, but the headline rank results are arithmetic, not evidence; the empirical content is the conditioning and noise comparison among IDENTIFIABLE designs (F-007), where photon counting is better than dual-kVp at equal basis size and equal photons. Spectral mismatch always biases a nominal-spectrum estimator (F-005); whether that bias is visible depends on the material scored, the dose and the statistic, which is a warning about evaluation design for H1/Q-002. Basis misspecification remains systematic and dose-independent (F-008). This episode is itself evidence that pre-registered criteria need a power analysis and an all-material scope before they are binding.
limitations: All prior limitations stand (idealised 2D toy, shared forward model for data and estimator, ray-subset statistics, D-002 iodine K-edge under-resolved, laptop CPU/MPS only, absolute spectrum normalisation unverified). Added: the emp/CRLB check cannot detect a wrong attenuation table or spectrum; equal-photon comparison excludes pure gain mismatch by construction; the energy-integrating Poisson model (noise applied to E-weighted counts) is idealised; headline recovery numbers (iodine RMSE 0.005 g/cm3 vs a 0.005 g/cm3 insert; calcium 0.085 vs 0.1-0.3) are NOT evidence of good recovery.
next_experiment: EXP-003 (revised by this review): spectral-mismatch bias study driven by DETERMINISTIC noise-free bias as the primary quantity, with Monte-Carlo only to establish detectability. Required design changes: score ALL materials, not iodine alone; pre-compute the detection floor and choose the realisation count from a power analysis BEFORE running; separate gain mismatch from shape mismatch; and compare against a first-order analytic bias prediction. Prerequisite for any inverse-crime-free comparison under H1.
unresolved: Whether photon counting retains its advantage once detector response, charge sharing and pile-up are modelled (all absent here). How conclusions move under a genuinely mismatched forward model (H1/Q-002). Whether the K-edge-resolved table (T-006) changes iodine conditioning.
what_failed: Three overstatements in my own original findings, all corrected: (1) F-001 presented rank results as empirical when rank<=min(n_meas,k) is forced by matrix shape, and quoted a 2.70x noise penalty for photon counting that confounded design with basis size - at equal basis size photon counting is 2.5x BETTER. (2) F-002 called an emp/CRLB agreement 'validation of the forward model' when it is a self-consistency check that a wrong table or spectrum would pass equally; the quoted 11% was actually 12.5%. (3) F-004 claimed dual-kVp was 'not detectably biased' under mismatch; a noise-free calculation shows bias is ALWAYS present, and the dual-kVp energy-scale case is clearly biased (4x floor). The pre-registered criterion was defective in two ways: iodine-only scoring, and requiring significance at both dose levels so the noisier level dominated. A unit mislabel (g/cm3 vs g/cm2) in the run metrics was also corrected.
what_happened: POST-REVIEW CORRECTION of the EXP-002 synthesis. An independent reviewer (who did not produce the work) challenged all four original findings; Opus verified each challenge against the raw metrics and by a new noise-free calculation. Three of four findings were superseded or amended. Current findings: F-005 (supersedes F-004), F-006 (supersedes F-002), F-007 (supersedes F-001), F-008 (amends F-003).
what_worked: Rank/identifiability verdicts are robust to the rank threshold over 1e-2..1e-10. Conditioning numbers and the misspecification result survived review. The mismatch implementation was audited and contains NO cancellation bug: the tilt is a shape change with mean-weighted factor ~1, so rescaling to equal photons removes only overall gain (a pure gain mismatch is excluded by design, which is a scope limit, not an error).

interpretation: The headline ranking is an artifact of the metric, not of method quality: simplex 'wins' by clipping unphysical boundary values, while sum_to_one - which solves the physics exactly where the model holds - comes last. Reporting s1 alone on a two-regime phantom would rank a clipped estimator above an exact one (F-016). This is a benchmark-design result that applies to the real AAPM data too, where boundary pixels are ~5% of the image.
limitations: SYNTHETIC DATA ONLY - no AAPM case data was processed, so no AAPM-dependent or leaderboard-comparable number exists. 32x32 vs the real 512x512; the official s1 divides by 3*512^2 so the magnitudes are not comparable. Image-domain only (no fan-beam projector, so the transmission-domain methods the winners used are untested). TV lam=1e-4 was picked by a coarse scan on the same synthetic problem, so its 36% gain is optimistic. AIR_CUTOFF_PER_CM=0.1 is a modelling choice untested on real data. No U-Net yet (T-012).
next_experiment: T-012 small U-Net on the same synthetic harness, evaluated against zero_prediction and classical_simplex on the SAME val split, with the test split untouched. Then the fan-beam projector needed for transmission-domain methods (the regime the published winners used).
unresolved: Whether the boundary pathology has the same magnitude on real AAPM data (boundary fraction and PSF differ). Whether a weighted-least-squares-over-simplex estimator (rather than projecting the sum_to_one solution) fixes the boundary regime. Whether image-domain methods can approach the published transmission-domain results at all.
what_failed: No pre-registered hypothesis was falsified (this was a diagnostic run, not a comparison). Three runs were wasted on a provenance defect: git_dirty was always true because Research OS logs into the repo during the run (F-017).
what_happened: RUN-0006 (source-clean, commit c4b043b, 4s CPU): 5 methods on 17 synthetic val cases (32x32, noiseless, AAPM schema, real CC-BY mu tables). s1: classical_simplex 0.0508 < classical_tv 0.0525 < classical_unconstrained 0.303 < zero_prediction 0.430 < classical_sum_to_one 1.179. Determinism confirmed: RUN-0003/4/5/6 produced identical metrics.
what_worked: Adapter, metrics, classical baseline and harness run end to end and are reproducible. Regime separation exposed what the pooled metric hid: sum_to_one is near-exact on tissue (RMSE 1.29e-6) and catastrophic on the boundary band (3.84, max 11.5).

interpretation: The headline claim is supported: a label-free consistency objective fits the measurements BETTER than methods that get the physics right, while being far more wrong about materials - low forward residual is not evidence of material accuracy. But the prior-ablation half of this experiment is inconclusive by my own design error, and the P2 inversion is unexplained. Scope: synthetic procedural phantoms, image domain, 32x32 - NOT AAPM data and NOT the projection domain the published winners used.
limitations: Synthetic data only; image domain only (no fan-beam projector exists, so no sinogram-domain conclusion is available); 13 val cases; 3 seeds; prior_weight fixed at 1.0 and never tuned; B2 early-stops on validation LABELS (disclosed); test split never loaded. Critically, the image-domain linear model these rungs assume is wrong by 6-8% on REAL AAPM images (F-025), so none of these numbers should be expected to transfer.
next_experiment: Do NOT rerun this ladder. The binding gap is the forward model: image-domain linear inversion is 6-8% wrong on real AAPM data, so the next experiment must be a fan-beam projector + projection-domain consistency, which is also the regime the published winners used.
unresolved: Why B3's material error is seed-STABLE while its consistency loss is seed-unstable (P2 inverted). Whether a properly weighted soft sum_to_one, or an occupancy-aware hard constraint, recovers the identifying power F-019/F-024 analyse. Why architectural softmax collapses to a constant map.
what_failed: P2 FAIL: B3's material error was NOT seed-unstable (cv 0.035, predicted >0.2) while its CONSISTENCY loss was (cv 0.61, predicted <0.05) - the exact opposite of my prediction, and I have no explanation yet; it suggests the implicit prior selects a consistent member of the ambiguous family rather than a random one. P3 FAIL and P5 FAIL are design errors of mine, not results (F-023): P3 tested a unit-weight SOFT penalty against the >5x effect F-019 proved for a HARD constraint, and I set no weight in the pre-registration. B4e/B4f (architectural softmax) collapsed to constant all-adipose maps on every seed.
what_happened: RUN-0008 (recorded, commit c461aa3, git_dirty_source=False, 85s CPU): 10 rungs x 3 seeds on 13 synthetic val cases, 32x32, image domain. Pre-registered STOP condition TRIGGERED (B3-linear tissue RMSE 0.476 vs best B4 0.468 = 1.02x, not the predicted >5x). Predictions: P1 PASS, P2 FAIL, P3 FAIL, P4 PASS, P5 FAIL, P6 reported, P7 PASS.
what_worked: P1 confirmed emphatically and is the main result: B3 attains the LOWEST consistency loss of all ten rungs (9.6e-5, 5x better than classical B0's 4.7e-4) while its tissue RMSE is 26x worse than B0 and 8.7x worse than supervised B2, with null|cos| 0.993. A capacity control (F-022) rules out undertraining: supervised saturates at 0.037 after 19x epochs and 4x capacity, so the network floor is only 7.8% of B3's error and the identifiability gap is 92%.

interpretation: PRELIMINARY, synthetic known-material disk phantoms only, XCIST as reference simulator (itself a model, not truth). (1) M1 small is a STRUCTURAL/adapter check (same transport equation), not independent validation. (2) The floor is dominated by object edges (max errors 0.4-0.8 in -ln units) and truth rasterisation, not a uniform offset. (3) Changing attenuation tables xraylib vs Geant4 EDLP97 moves projections ~0.1-0.2% - negligible next to the rest. (4) The spectral specification is the largest single mismatch (~2-2.6%, systematic). These are two different physical spectrum specifications (XCIST tungsten_tar7.0 filt files vs spectra_v1 SpekPy with unverified filtration), so this quantifies sensitivity to spectrum specification, not an error of either.
limitations: Only the single-ray central-ray XCIST model; 1 row; no scatter (XCIST scatter model not exercised); energy-integrating detector only - NO photon-counting response compared; M3 uses XCIST's own weights as the 'detector' reference so it measures only absorption/prefilter; reconstruction domain not compared; disks only (no heterogeneity); one geometry (SID 540/SDD 950); XCIST uses 20 equal 6 keV bins internally and we reuse that quadrature in every stage (shared approximation). Bins below 10 keV dropped (weight fraction <=1e-11).
next_experiment: HPC replication of a small XCIST run via native protocol (needs Python>=3.10 env on cluster); then Experiment E1 supervised baseline on these records.

interpretation: Under the shared physical model (official spectra, attenuation tables, geometry, I0=1, noiseless), our projector+polychromatic forward reproduces the official generator's transmissions to float32 rounding, on the kit and dataset cases. The observed error is ~3.3x below the pre-derived tolerance (tolerance was derived first from float32 propagation, not from these errors). The official layered projector is exactly the exact-chord integral. This is implementation fidelity against the official generator; it says nothing about real-scanner accuracy, noise, scatter or spectrum error. Gate passed: physics-loss training may proceed.
limitations: Errors by angle/detector/occupancy are saved (exp017_profiles.npz, rows json) but not individually interpreted here; 40 dataset cases are a stride sample not all 1000; chord-vs-layered comparison is at 64^2/128^2 (dense 512^2 infeasible), on one kit case; peak memory/runtime are for inference only, not backward.

interpretation: Successful gradient flow is not successful recovery. Label-free projection consistency produced a collapsed, anatomically empty adipose/fibroglandular mixture (s1 13x worse than supervised) while its projection error was only 1.7x worse; 99.7% of its material error lies along the F-012 null direction (isotropic reference ~0.5). This matches the pre-registered expectation from F-014 (null direction invisible to the data) but is a single seed and 8 val cases, descriptive only. The sum<=1 hinge (feasibility only) did not help and worsened s1 (0.50): a weak feasibility constraint does not select the truth. Calcification RMSE 0.010 in all arms is NOT recovery evidence: calcification covers ~0.4% of pixels, and predicting zero scores about this value.
limitations: One seed; 32 training / 8 validation cases; short training; the supervised arm's own error is also 84% along the null direction; the physics arms' hyperparameters (lr, views per step) were not tuned; same-model data (no mismatch).

interpretation: All image-domain classical methods are poor on the real AAPM images: best (TV) s1 0.271 is only 1.6x better than predicting nothing (0.446), against supervised U-Net s1 0.016 (EXP-022 seed 2) and the published winners ~1e-6 scale. Pre-registered expectations hold on 100 cases: raw sum_to_one is 3.4x WORSE than the zero prediction (cond~1273 amplifies the reconstruction/beam-hardening model mismatch; consistent with F-025/F-027), and simplex projection (0.381) is worse than the raw unconstrained pinv (0.315). Constraints do not help merely because they are physical: simplex raises boundary error (0.48 vs 0.26 unconstrained). TV lowers interior RMSE (0.33 vs 0.40) but raises boundary RMSE (0.41 vs 0.26) and s2 (0.66 vs 0.43). Calcification is near-trivially small (RMSE 0.004-0.014).
limitations: Validation only; image-domain linear model ignores beam hardening (same-image approach as F-025); grid edge saturation; single air-cutoff value; no nonlinear projection-domain method here (planned as a separate experiment); statements about ranking among close methods (nonneg 0.307 vs unconstrained 0.315) are not tested for significance (per-case values saved).
next_experiment: Projection-domain iterative baseline (new experiment); final test evaluation of all methods at the end of the benchmark.
